designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch the pre-allocated blocks and the structure that hands them out without a general-purpose allocator. Then, thinking ahead to allocate-on-thread-A / free-on-thread-B, sketch what would have to be true for a free block to be invisible to the other thread until a cache spills. Name the central structure and the per-thread structure.
requiredElements: per-thread cache versus central stack named

parts.title: Fixed-capacity allocate / release

hints.text: How do you hand out at most `capacity` blocks, and get one back, without allocating after construction?
Pre-create `capacity` bytearrays and keep the unused ones on a stack. allocate pops; release pushes.
self._free = [bytearray(block_size) for _ in range(capacity)]. allocate returns pop() or None; release appends the block back.

probes: Why a pool instead of `bytearray(block_size)` on every allocate?
What happens to a block's contents when it is released and then reallocated?

parts.title: Double-free and unknown-block detection

hints.text: A free-list of unused blocks cannot tell a second release of the same block from a first one. What extra set would?
Track currently-live identities. allocate adds; release removes. A release whose identity is not live is the error.
Keep self._live = set of id(block) (or the objects themselves). release: if id(block) not in _live: raise; else discard and push onto the free-list.

probes: Thread-local free list versus a lock-free central stack — what bug does the live-set still catch?
How would you detect use-after-free in a debug build without slowing the hot path in release builds?

parts.title: Thread-local cache, spill to central

hints.text: If every release goes to one global stack, the other thread can allocate it immediately. What extra place could a release sit that only its own thread looks at first?
Per-thread stack of at most cache_size blocks. allocate: pop local, else pop central. release: push local if room, else push central.
self._caches: thread -> list, plus self._central. cache_size 0 means every release goes central (part 1). Default thread=0 so allocate()/release(block) keep working.

probes: Why might you *want* a free block to be invisible to the other thread for a while?
Alignment / cache-line padding on pool metadata versus payload — what false sharing are you avoiding?

criteria: cached free blocks are not allocated by a different thread until spill
live-set sits beside the free-list rather than replacing it
thread cache is an extra place a block can sit, not a second pool of capacity
identity (id or object) used for live tracking, not a copy of the bytes
double-free and cross-thread invisibility considered before being told
stated why a local cache can make allocate() return None for the other thread
